title: Graph neural network enables first observation of Λc⁺ → ne⁺νe decay
summary: Using 4.5 fb⁻¹ of BESIII electron–positron collision data, the collaboration reports the first observation of the Cabibbo-suppressed Λc⁺ → ne⁺νe decay at greater than 10σ significance. It measures a branching fraction of (3.57 ± 0.34(stat) ± 0.14(syst)) × 10⁻³ and extracts |Vcd| = 0.208 ± 0.011(exp) ± 0.007(LQCD) ± 0.001(lifetime) for the first time from a charmed-baryon decay.
ai_technology: Graph neural network (GNN) trained on BESIII electromagnetic-calorimeter shower patterns

evidence.tested: Using 4.5 fb⁻¹ of BESIII electron–positron collision data, the collaboration reports the first observation of the Cabibbo-suppressed Λc⁺ → ne⁺νe decay at greater than 10σ significance.
evidence.unknown: The observation is an experimental result from the BESIII data sample; the branching-fraction and |Vcd| uncertainties include statistical, systematic, lattice-QCD and lifetime components as reported. The paper studies data-versus-simulation domain shift and network uncertainty; residual modeling differences contribute to systematic uncertainty. The |Vcd| extraction depends on lattice-QCD input.
evidence.ai_role: The GNN separated neutron signal showers from the dominant Λc⁺ → Λe⁺νe background, whose neutron-plus-π⁰ calorimeter patterns are difficult to distinguish with conventional selection or boosted trees. The authors trained and calibrated it using large J/ψ control samples, then fitted its output distributions to extract the signal yield.
